title: Notes of Ministry - 6 - May 1973

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 6 - May 1973 (2030)/Notes of Ministry - 6 - May 197 - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: We have had this verse before us today and yesterday, yet I feel impressed to dwell upon it, because of the pointed urgency of seizing the great issues of a positive kind which are involved in this present moment. Times sometimes come when we may need, with the help of the Spirit, to break through the detail of current things that may have engaged us closely, to see the great ultimate end which is in mind in all the detail. What has impressed me in reading back into the great ministries which the Spirit so signally used is the place the assembly had in the affections and minds of those who have served us.

Those ministries have not left us ignorant, speaking generally, as to teaching concerning the assembly. There is not, in general, great lack of knowledge as to what is suited to the service of God. But what the Spirit of God is getting at relates to the deeper roots of devotion to Christ, and of longing for what befits Christ, that develop as our hearts and renewed minds are filled with that Man. We are then brought to realise, not so much by the detail of the teaching, but by depth of conviction that the Spirit would impart to us, that the securing of a vessel, a creature vessel suited to Christ, is the great point of this wonderful time of the Spirit.

I would ask myself what conviction I have as to the assembly. We know the term; we use it often; we speak of it; we sing hymns of it. Thank God, we touch the features of the service that relate to it; but the root being tested out—which will still be tested out—is that depth of conviction in devotion to Christ that cherishes what fully answers to His heart. As He has it, what an outcome there is for God—I say that, that we may realise the place that the assembly has, and is to have, in the final filling out of what is eternally to God’s glory. The assembly united to Christ, and moving under His headship, will fill out the whole scene as that in which the blessed God substantiates what answers to Himself, to His own blessed heart.

But what is in mind, beloved brethren, in all this is the greatest refinement. A chaste virgin presented to Christ represents a kind of essence of refinement in a creature vessel, a vessel which is in view in our present service. It is a vessel which is to be rightly brought into substantial expression as we continue together in numbers which may be very small, or small, or not quite so small, but never large, in our time. In its refined character, detached from everything that relates to man in sin, it is presented for the heart of Christ to delight Him, so that the Lord can take His place in view of what goes forward for the pleasure of God.

What are our convictions.as to Christ and as to the assembly? Have we yet drunk into the quality and character of that love, known as it springs up in the heart of the heavenly Man, that seeks, whatever the cost, a suited answer to itself? And if something of that love has affected us, to what lengths are we ready to go in committal, that such an answer as that might be secured?

Therefore the writer here speaks of his jealousy. “I am jealous”, he says, “as to you”. What an expression of the depth of feeling of the beloved apostle—“Jealous as to you”, he says. That is, he has no formal objective, would emphasise, no formal objective. He is not filling out a kind of formality of service; he is thinking of what is for Christ, seizing the full character that must attach to it, if it is to be truly for Christ. He is allowing no reduction in his mind and heart of the refined quality of that which must be secured to afford a full answer to Him. But he is labouring to that end. He had a hard time, did he not? His was no easy path of service. Even when he went to Corinth, I suppose relatively early in the history of the place, it was with fear and much trembling. How he felt things in that city! You wonder what the cause of his fear was. I would think, from the way he presents it, that it was not the fear of man as such; it would be the fear of the subtlety of the foe spoiling what God would work out in that city, in the midst of all its corruptions. How he felt these things. His heart was just in tune, in harmony, with the heart of an exalted Christ, a Man in the glory. He was labouring in the gain of all that is set forth, for him and for us, in that Man.

Are our engagements with Christ in heaven sufficiently frequent and sufficiently extended? Are we ready just to ponder, and still ponder, and still ponder, what is up there in that glorious Man, and be affected by it? Is our view of Christ extending? Are we getting enriched thoughts about Him? If not, what is standing in the way?’ Our flesh will always stand in the way; it will always do so, if it is allowed. What is of man and his world will always stand in the way, if it is allowed. We shall never gain expansion in these things as occupied with the passing matters of man’s world. We have to walk in soberness, and work in soberness, in the midst of current affairs; but what is our absorbing engagement in these closing moments of the richest time of all in God’s ways in blessing? Shall we let the closing moments pass, beloved brethren, without getting the simple point of them? That point, I believe, is conveyed to us in these brief verses we have read. Shall we come out in Pauline character, or shall we come out in some other character? If so, what character is it? Is it a character that God is pleased with? Is it a character as to which God might say, Here is a man in the full, rich current of My mind and thoughts? You and I, any of us here—elderly ones here, young ones here can just go forward in the full current of God’s mind and thoughts. He has no thought otherwise for us.

Shall we yield, shall we move on in these things, or is some passing thing hindering us? Am I a self-centred person, thinking of things as they affect me? How many of us have had to face and see what that really means, to get self-centred, and relate everything to ourselves. God has just to come in and say, I am not going to have that. God must be the Centre of the realm into which He has come. It must be so. He has set a glorious Man. His beloved Son, as the Centre of His world, and God is committed to that. It is a simple touch, I know, but if what we bring forward, if what we make our objective, is out of accord with the Son of God, God will have to disallow it. He is committed to the establishment of everything in relation to His beloved Son.

So, dear brethren, let us cultivate what is refined. Let us repudiate the small things, the trivial things, the things maybe that have grown and grown and grown in our minds, because of self-occupation. Let us see them, and judge them, and set them aside, that we may arrive at the true level of Paul, of divine refinement, which God is at in our time. I would love to think that we get a view of Christ in that connection. Think of the awful corruption of man’s world into which He came—right into the heart of it. He came.

What there was in that precious Babe, “the holy thing”, as the scripture says; something that nothing of man could contaminate or reduce in its infinite perfection. Luke presents Him growing; a boy of twelve; a man beginning to be about thirty years of age; and what came into expression in that Man was absolute refinement according to God. Think of that scene in the Pharisee’s house in Luke 7. How Luke delights to present the refinement of things in Christ in view of the understanding of what belongs in the assembly. That Pharisee, thinking critically within himself, had his own thoughts, which were diverse from the great point of the occasion. So the woman appears, a repenting woman. The Lord calls attention to her; He commends her, and He sends her away in peace. Things are kept on a level of moral refinement, with the perfection of Jesus there. The utter degradation of man in flesh is evident, but Jesus comes into the totally dominant relation of the whole episode. He sends that woman away in peace but never abrogates divine standards; He does not pass by the history of that woman in sin, to which the Pharisee calls attention, but provides for it in accomplishing redemption. There is for men forgiveness of sins, peace, the gift of the Spirit, that this refined level of things should go on.

So it was as the Lord was among His beloved disciples; you see it running right through the gospels. Just take account of the moral perfections of Jesus, in the midst of all the corruptions of man in his affairs; you see there what the divine point is in the suggestion of what is so intrinsically precious and refined, “to present you a chaste virgin to Christ”. We have the hint of it, of course, in many previous passages; the mind turns to David, fuming as he went to slay a man who had offended him, and being met by Abigail, who brought the discerning, refined touch to bear upon David; thank God, he answered to it, showing how these refined elements of things work as they are brought into view in the assembly. I fear—and the fear springs from what I find in myself—that the assembly has become almost a word in our vocabulary, when what the Spirit of God would have it to be is the great, substantial, divinely-adorned objective of all that He is carrying through to completion in the latter moments of His sojourn down here. We are to take on the spirit of that, dear brethren. My intention was to be brief, and that is what I had to say; but I believe we need to heed the peculiar character and force of this verse in this time—to which we have come, that we do not lose the life-stream of this wonderful time of revival in which our God has called us.

May we take on these things, and, if we have never done it before, continue in whatever may be opened up to us by way of service or activity in the assembly, to have the full divine objective in view.

Brethren will note that each of these scriptures refers to what is daily. You will recall that during the reading meeting Mr. Widtfeldt referred to the side of what goes on with us daily, every day, in connection with what we had been speaking of, our consecrating ourselves and devoting ourselves to be here for the pleasure of God. This matter of making a vow to commit ourselves to the testimony of God and to the will of God, and to the pleasure of our Lord Jesus Christ, is really based on daily entering into the blessings that are ours; daily entering into the exercises which are vital for us to have, as Christians, and daily being dependent on God for all that we need and all that is to be obtained through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

So I have read these scriptures, which all refer to things going on daily, in view of encouraging our hearts that christianity is a daily matter. I know that it has been said that christianity is a weekly matter. That is true, too, from the standpoint of the weekly cycle of things in the assembly. In the days of the Israelites it tended to be more of a monthly matter.

Things were done by months, certain months being the time for certain feasts. Christianity has become more of a weekly matter. Things are carried out through the week with other believers, as we assemble together to carry out what we call the weekly calendar. But as to myself, as a christian, having committed myself to the testimony for carrying it through, having committed myself to the will of God, to see that I am moving in His will, and having committed myself to be here for the pleasure of my Lord and Saviour, christianity becomes a daily matter. That is, you and I and all christians are to take up our responsibilities, our exercises and our privileges every day. So I read these scriptures trusting that a few words relating to them will just help us to see how certain aspects of daily christianity are involved in our individual pathways.

A great deal is being made by some of what is individual, and this is quite all right if held properly in relation to God’s thoughts about the assembly. There is the individual side of things which must go on with us each day, and at the same time there is what is true of us in a collective sense. So we must see that God is working to the end of having the assembly as a collective entity, for His glory eternally. We were speaking at the end of the last meeting of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus as really connected with what is collective. But there is the high calling connected with us as individuals, as called into christianity to be individually linked with God. Individually, on the basis of the blood of Christ, each of us is linked with God and that eternally. Eternally I am called to sonship, a wonderful thing, for no greater calling could be conferred on a man than to be called a son of God. If your calling was that of a nobleman or you were chosen to be in the cabinet of the President of this country it would be a very high calling, but there is no calling equal to that of the believer.

The cabinet members of the President may serve for four years, some will have served longer than that at the end of their term. Their calling has been high, in time, but our calling, beloved brethren, as christians, into the glorious privilege and place of sonship, is eternal. It is not to end in four years, because our King is in power for ever. His place, as enthroned, is never to be taken away from Him, nor will He be voted out of power. You and I have the place of noblemen, called to that place in sonship, to be associated with Christ for ever. Oh what a high calling that is!

The high calling also is collective. It is wonderful that God has called us to have part in the assembly, where, as the collective totality of His work. His glory will be enshrined and be radiant for ever. How wonderful that is! Think of that, God’s glory shining in the saints for ever! Oh, what a calling that is, and we have been called into that. I know that there are many who are discouraged at the present time, so many have a tendency to turn away back from the rigours and exercises that are involved in the testimony. But oh, if we could all get the vision before our souls of what the calling on high of God is and what our future is, as christians, and what it involves for us eternally, I believe none would ever pull back or go away. I believe that. I believe if we had that vision soberly and permanently in our souls “the calling on high of God in Christ Jesus”, involving these great and eternal realities, we would never go away. And, dear brethren, let us take courage from these things. If anyone is discouraged with the smallness of things at the present time, with the trial of jealousy that the Lord has brought in to refine things, oh, take courage from the calling which you have been brought into, the calling of God in Christ Jesus, for you as an individual and for you as having part in the assembly.

Well, the scriptures read do not exactly relate to what I have just been saying, except that we take up these things individually, on a daily basis, and apart from that I believe there will be something lacking with us. Apart from daily being involved in the exercises and privileges of being a christian, we will be lacking something and God also will be lacking something. Because if I lack in my response to God, if I lack in my testimony amongst men, if I lack in my living response which is due to God in the assembly, then God misses out. He lacks, because that is robbing God of what is due to Him from me as an individual.

So these persons in Acts 17 are said to be noble, which is a very interesting thing, as it links on with what we were saying as to the calling; but these persons were said to be noble by reason of what they were doing, not just noble by reason of the calling which was theirs.

They were called by the glad tidings that Paul preached amongst them, called to be christians, called into sonship, called into the favour of being in the family of God. But that is not just what the nobility of the Bereans relates to. They were noble from the standpoint of God’s calling, and no greater nobility could have been conferred upon them; but they were more noble than others because every day they were searching out the scriptures to see if christianity was a substantial reality. That, I believe, beloved brethren, is needed by all of us.

If we have made any kind of a committal to God, any, kind of a vow to God, this searching of the scriptures is a vital matter, every day. I think it is a need among us, because I see more and more that there are those who get discouraged and turn away from the truth and the rigours of the testimony, because of a lack in their souls. You may say; “Oh yes, they have this to complain about and that to complain about”. That may be true, for you can always find things to complain about. If you look very carefully at me, you will find a lot to complain about, because there is much of the flesh still residing in me, I know that, so if you watch me constantly you will find that to complain about; the way I do things, the way I say things, the way I carry myself amongst the brethren or in the testimony. Complain and complain as the Israelites did, but the truth usually is that if I become a complainer, there is a lack in my soul of links rightly held with Christ. If I continue as a complainer the enemy has a handle and will use it to get me soon to become a ridiculer, and soon to become a railer, and then the devil has won the day.

Well, these Bereans evidently were not occupied too much with one another or with complaints, because they took up the scriptures with readiness of mind and searched out the truth every day, to see that the things spoken by Paul were realities. Let us be on this line, beloved brethren, because it is a secret to soul progress. Take up the scriptures on a daily basis. It does not indicate that they just read them in a casual way, as you might read a newspaper, or perhaps your studies at school. It means that they were really looking for the truth of the scriptures, to see what Paul was preaching to them and that what Paul was teaching them was verily so, “searching the scriptures if these things were so”, searching them. Well, this is needed amongst us, to search things out. I had to search to find the scriptures I read, which relate to this word “daily”. We need to search things out and the Spirit of God helps us to do that. You will find that there are the depths of God in the Scriptures. What is said of the Spirit Himself is that He “searches all things, even the depths, of God” (1 Corinthians 2: 10). How does He do it? He knows the depths of God; the Spirit of God is God, so He knows them fully. Then how does He search them out? I believe He searches them out as you and I are exercised to go in for the truth and He reveals to us some of the deepest things of God’s treasure house.

That is what made these persons noble, and I believe it is what will make all of us noble, if we pursue this exercise on a regular, daily basis. Taking up the scriptures, not reading them in a casual way, but with readiness of mind, as is indicated with these Bereans “receiving the word with all readiness of mind”. It does not say they had little reserves about certain things which Paul said. We may do that; we may have little reserves about what a certain brother says; but they were receiving it with readiness of mind. Now I know that we got caught in erroneous things in the last 10 or 12 years by being on the line of receiving, as subject to persons, but that is not normal. The normal thing is that you are receiving what comes to you in the way of testimony and then you search it out to see that these things are so. That could be where we failed, in that period of time, by not searching out to see if what was ministered was the truth.

Then I have read in Proverbs about a man who was blessed. This relates to Mr. Hunziker’s reference in the reading meeting to Psalm 1, “Blessed is the man”. These are scriptures which we ought to search out as to what God says about a man that is blessed. Psalm 1 is one of them and here in Proverbs 8 is another, “Blessed is the man”, which includes woman also.

That does not just mean the masculine side, but blessed any person “that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors”. Now I know this scripture is concerning wisdom. It is all about wisdom and how to get wisdom and it is wisdom speaking, wisdom personified speaking, as to how a man is blessed, watching at wisdom’s gates, waiting at the posts of wisdom’s doors, to get wisdom. But I want to apply it to Christ personally, although I know it has been said that you cannot exactly apply this great matter of wisdom as being Christ specifically, but I believe that through this scripture He would speak to us. Through this scripture the Lord Jesus would say to us by the Holy Spirit, ‘Blessed is the man who heareth Me’. I believe it is very true that a man is blessed as he is at the gates of wisdom day by day, looking to see how he can become wiser. But I think for a Christian it involves being daily at the gates, looking for a way of entering into the things of God as associated with Christ Himself. “My gates”, it says, “Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates”. Those are Christ’s gates, that open up into a sphere where Christ is, as exalted, where He is known. There is such a sphere where He is exalted, where everything bows in homage to Jesus. There are gates into that sphere. Are we exercised to be at those gates every day, not just a few times a week?

Some people tend just to live on the meetings. This you cannot do successfully in a spiritual way. This matter is for everyone, individually in their own exercises, to get to the gates where Christ is known, where there is an entrance into a sphere where He is exalted. “Blessed is the man that heareth me”. Well, how do you hear the Lord? How do you get any communication from the Lord at the present time? Is it not by taking time to read the scriptures, as we were saying, on a daily basis and to meditate and to give time for the Spirit of God to give impressions as to the voice of the Son of God? Is that not the way we hear His voice, through our meditations, through our thinking on lines connected with divine things, is that not how we hear Christ speaking? We do not have the opportunity to sit at Jesus’ feet in a literal way, as Mary did. We do not have the wondrous privilege which she had literally, but we do have that privilege spiritually, by the Spirit. Just taking time out, whatever your busy routine is each day, taking time out at the beginning of the day, in the middle of the day, or at the end of the day. Whenever you can find time, take a few moments, just to sit and meditate on divine things. This is being at His gates, that gives opportunity to hear His voice, to hear His words, and I believe none will be disappointed. I believe the Holy Spirit will always give you something. Make up your mind that you are going to use a little time, it may be only a few moments, in which you hunt for something that relates to the glory of Christ, in the sphere where He is honoured, where He is made much of. Oh what a sphere that is! We shall soon be there actually, beloved brethren: We shall soon be in that sphere for ever, where Christ is made much of in everything and in all.

“For whoso findeth me findeth life”. Have we found that in our own experience? Just to find Christ as our Saviour is a great matter. You have found life if you have found Jesus as your Saviour; you have found life already. What happens to so many Christians is that they settle down with that assurance; but the man that is blessed of Jehovah is the man that is daily at the gates, seeking His words and finding there something that refreshes his soul, so that he is a living person, day by day. Not only that he has the promise of life eternally, but that he is living every day in relation to God. Well, that is what this scripture contemplates, persons daily involved in finding resource and sustenance at the gates where all the resource comes from. You know, we tend to find resource in things of this life. There is a day coming soon when everything of this life will be finished. Your job will be finished, your schooling will be finished, everything you are connected with now, even the mercies which God gives us to enjoy, your family, your children, your parents, friends, etc. There will be no more resource from those things at all in the eternal day. No one will go to jobs in the day of eternity and find resource there, no one will go back to their own family and find resource, comfort and encouragement. All our resource will flow from Christ personally. Are we living on that resource now? Let us do it daily, for this source of refreshment, source of encouragement, source of strength for the journey, will be found as we hear His words.

Now I read the other two scriptures, in Matthew and Luke, because they are the Lord’s own words. In Matthew 6 the Lord is instructing His disciples on how to pray. They asked Him how to pray and that was a good desire, to learn how to pray. So the Lord is very explicit with His disciples as to how to pray. I am not going to go into the detail here. What I want to concentrate on is what He says in verses 9, 10 and 11, “Thus therefore pray ye—Our Father who art in the heavens, let thy name be sanctified, let thy kingdom come, let thy will be done as in heaven so upon the earth; give us today our needed bread, and forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors”. I think that little word in there, “today”, “give us today our needed bread”, indicates that the Lord is contemplating that we would be praying every day.

It shows that I am to pray for today. Tomorrow as it may come, through mercy, I shall pray for tomorrow, and the next day I shall pray for that day. “Give us today” shows that the Lord is looking for this, a daily kind of dependence on the part of His people. It becomes a test, therefore, Am I depending on God, depending on the Father? Wonderful how the Lord Jesus speaks of your Father (verse 8); not My Father here, but your Father. He is saying to His disciples, and He wants to impress us, I believe, with the fact that God is our Father. So the prayer begins that way, “Our Father who art in the heavens”.

It is very striking, as has been often pointed out, that the Lord is really indicating that the first thing that should be in our minds is how God is to be glorified in everything. So He says that the prayer should begin, “Our Father … let thy name be sanctified … let thy will be done”. Is that the way we start our prayers, beloved brethren? I do not mean just saying these words. I know that there are many christians who read this as a text, and this becomes their prayer.

Well, they do not realise that they are guilty of the very thing which the Lord says should not be done, vain repetition. So if you just read a prayer it becomes vain repetition. Even this fine prayer, this exalted matter which the Lord is teaching them, if you just read it every day, is vain repetition; that is all it is. But we are thinking of God first in our prayers, of His glory, that His Name may be sanctified, that His will may be done. This is to show that the believer thinks first for God and His rights, what is due unto Him, every day. Think of what is due to God right today. Every breath should be praising God, every breath, because every breath that a man breathes is given by God. So every person in the world ought to be praising and thanking God today. The rain which came down last night was for everyone; it rains on the just and the unjust alike. The crops that grow as a result of the rain are for everyone; so thanksgiving is due to God from every man. What if God withheld the rain, for two or three years? What if He withheld it for five years all over this continent? What would happen? Think of that! God is due thanksgiving from every man, just or unjust. Well, let us render to God what is due to Him every day.

“Let thy will be done” shows we are submitting to God’s will. Whatever happens today, we are submissive to it, we are prepared for God’s will. Whether peace comes in Viet Nam, or whether it does not, God’s will is involved. We know that the President of this country is striving for peace, but it is not depending on his will. It is the same with every matter, with national or international affairs, and with matters that relate to God’s people, it is all connected with God’s will. Whatever is done, we know for God’s people that is the best, “Let thy will be done”.

Then He says, “Give us today our needed bread”. Oh what a matter that is—It shows that we just must be dependent in everything. You know God could take the life or health of any of us at any moment. You might say, I have plenty of money, I have a good job, and I have no problem in getting food for my family. Well I meet people every week who do not work every day, and they cannot work every day because their health is gone. Some do not know where the next meal is going to come from. Now that is a solemn thing to think about, because that could be true of any one of us. “Give us today our needed bread” shows we are depending on the Father for what we have every day.

More than that, I believe the Lord would have in mind our depending on Him for our spiritual needs, food from heaven to fill our souls. Are we doing that? You know, as the children of Israel walked through the wilderness, every day there was some bread that came down from heaven. It covered the wilderness every morning. And it says in Exodus 16 they were to go out daily and gather the manna and they were to eat that day what they gathered. They were not to store it up, they were to live on it that day. It shows that daily exercise is needed by the christian to get as a resource what will feed his soul. Am I counting on God for it? Have I some impressions today of His wondrous grace, of divine love, some impression of Christ, His beloved Son, to feed my soul as a resource today?

We will not go into further details of the prayer, as I want to refer to Luke chapter 9, where we read. This is a very testing matter. I do not believe any of us will be prepared for what the Lord is saying here in Luke 9 unless we have been daily pursuing the scriptures and daily seeking a word from the Lord to engage us, and daily found in dependence on God.

Otherwise we will not be prepared for the test that is put to us here. I wonder how many christians are prepared for this, “If anyone will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me”. We all in this room ought to be prepared for this test, because of the greatness of the truth that is available to us, the fulness of the ministry under which we have sat for years; but yet, perhaps we are not. Now we sing that hymn, “Saviour we long to follow Thee”, and I believe we all mean that. The hymn was written by a very spiritual man, and I believe this would show what a spiritual test this is, really to follow Jesus.

It says, “If anyone will come after me”. Whenever you get this in scripture, “anyone”, it is a general divine principle applying to everyone. So, if anyone follows Jesus, this is what he must do. He must take up his cross daily. People speak about divine principles and sometimes they do not know what they are, but here is one divine principle. The Lord was just telling His disciples where He was going, to the cross, to be rejected of the elders, chief priests and scribes, and to be killed. He knew what His cross involved and He is able to speak about it, with a fulness that none other knew. Then He says, “Let him deny himself and take up his cross”. Does this just mean every week when you remember the Lord, or once a year when you might make a new year’s resolution? No, daily, every day; take up your cross daily. It means that I am prepared for the same kind of reproach, prepared to be rejected in this world; because He goes on to say, “Whosoever shall desire to save his life shall lose it”.

That means, I believe, simply, if I am prepared to follow Jesus, I am prepared to give up my life in this world, give up my reputation, give up the honour that I might think is due to me, prepared to be reproached for His Name, prepared to be rejected of men around, relatives, whoever it might be, for Jesus’ sake. That is what taking up my cross involves, and that is what Jesus is saying to His own here, not once a year, but daily. Are we prepared for that every day? I believe we can be prepared for that, on the basis of committing ourselves, devotedly, as we have had in the reading meeting today, in a consecrated way, as Nazarites, to read the scriptures, search them daily; to be at wisdom’s gates where Christ is and to hear His words, and to be daily depending on God the Father for every resource, material and spiritual. Then we will be prepared to take up the cross daily and follow Jesus. Whether it involves rejection and sorrow today, whether tomorrow it involves reproach from others, whether it involves that some of the persons nearest and dearest to me say, “Oh he is just too devoted”, or whatever it is, I am prepared for that, to take up my cross.

I do not believe the Lord is here referring to deprivation and suffering which the saints might go through in their bodies. Sometimes it is referred to in this way. People go through suffering in their bodies and it is a cross they bear; but I do not believe the Lord is at that matter here. I believe He is at the matter of our being like Himself, prepared for sacrifice, prepared for reproach and rejection in the world, prepared to lose our life in this world, so that we might gain life in Christ’s world.

Well, may these things encourage our hearts. They are very testing; they are very testing to me, for christianity is testing, but it has its wondrous reward in fruit for our souls, and that will be for eternity. All that we enjoy now we will enjoy in fulness for eternity. But the Lord would compensate us now. Every person holding himself energetically for the testimony of our Lord Jesus, and in relation to divine interests, the Lord will compensate. When I read Mr. J. N. Darby’s letters I wonder at what that man went through, and yet there is such an evidence of the compensation which he received in his links with divine Persons. There was such fulness of impressions, and glorious living realities were there in his soul as a result of all that he was prepared to deny himself of. Daily he took up his cross, faithfully to the end.
So let us be encouraged, beloved brethren, as we have our links together. Though the path is rigorous, let us be prepared for going in for divine things, for Christ’s name’s sake.

I think it is a time particularly for prophecy, but also for young men who see visions, and for elders who dream dreams in the spiritual sense and meaning. As would be evident, the apostle, quoting Joel, is applying it to the time, as indeed it referred to the time, of the incoming of the blessed Spirit. He quotes it in explanation of what was happening. He was testifying, and his testimony was effective, as the latter part of the chapter shows; and it went on being effective. Day by day the Lord added. In the fulness of what he quotes, it waits for a coming day. But it has its bearing upon the present day. We are acquainted with the matter of prophecy. We thank God for it, and that we come together to make way for it. Every week it comes into our assembly calendar—we can thank God for that.

It may be very testing for some brethren where there are so very few, perhaps two only—you would need two, according to Paul. To continue week after week is very testing. We find it so with three or four, so it must be very testing for two. But, testing as it is, we find it a blessed experience that the Lord and the Spirit come in. How the sisters feel about it I do not know altogether—I know about some. It is more testing, perhaps, for the sisters than it is for the brothers. I think it is a very particular feature that we should all be together in it, brothers and sisters. We should be marked by faith as to the meeting. 1 Corinthians 14 shows that it is the Lord’s commandment that it should come into the assembly calendar. It is not just like an address; it is something different. Everybody needs to be in definite exercise about it; in faith about it. Then there would be removed any fear of criticism, or any impression conveyed of boredom—I do not suppose that it happens in these parts, but it might, on the part of the sisters, especially if there are only two brothers.

The thing to have in mind is that it is prophecy, that is, that God’s mind for the moment for the locality is to come out, and that involves that everybody is exercised as to conditions in the locality. A brother cannot get God’s mind unless he is exercised about conditions in his own locality. What is effected by it, only God knows. How little is effected by it may be our feeling, and that calls for much more exercise because it is a means that the Lord has for conveying what His mind is as to what is needed in the locality. And then there must be vessels available to convey His mind. Of course, He is sovereign and can use an ass, as He has done; but I think He would rather use a sensitive vessel, if there is one available. Again, the prophetic word is intended to edify and to encourage and console. Nothing new in all this, you say, but I think the Lord would encourage the brethren to continue, if possible, every week.

But then this scripture is not speaking about the meeting for prophetic ministry. It is speaking about “all flesh”, God pouring of His Spirit upon all flesh. It is speaking about sons and daughters prophesying. Sons do sometimes, perhaps, in the meeting, but this scripture does not refer to the meeting specifically—it would include the meeting, no doubt, but it is wider.

It is a good thing to hear a son, or a daughter, prophesying. It suggests the younger ones; it does not suggest the older ones, I think. And I would desire power to encourage the younger brothers and sisters as to this matter, not to remove it from them and say, Well, this certainly does not apply to us; we are young; it is not expected of us. Perhaps it is not expected of young people—the more is the pity! If it were expected, if it were prayed for (I am not asking any brother to pray publicly about it), but if it were expected, and prayed for, maybe it would come.

Young people—and some older ones—have plenty of conversation about things that are passing; but have they any conversation about the things of God? It is a great challenge for most of us as to the extent to which we speak of “the great things of God” (Acts 2: 11). That is what persons heard in Jerusalem; they heard in their own dialect these men speaking the great things of God. And they knew that there were certain persons there of whom they could ask questions, that is, about the great things of God. Asking questions about other things, of course, we are very familiar with; but there are not too many questions asked about the great things of God; there could be a good many more. In some meetings it would be a good thing if there were more questions asked, and a few less observations, perhaps; questions that would come from a need, and a desire, from an appetite, a hungering and thirsting after righteousness, which the Lord spoke of these would be very profitable questions. Questions can be unprofitable; but it might well be that there could be more questions.

In this chapter persons knew to whom to direct their questions. Perhaps you feel that there is nobody in the locality to whom to direct the questions; but you can still ask questions—even if you think that you are the brother who knows the most, you could ask the brother whom you think does not know nearly as much! Ask him a few questions—you would be surprised what can come out.

What I am thinking of particularly is not only prophecy, which is so important, but the young men seeing visions—and the older men are not left out. I suppose the suggestion is that the older men would not be so active; but I think that the dreams that they would have would be very profitable ones. And what they have learned in their dreams would come out. All depends upon the presence of God in the Spirit, the Spirit of God. This was the occasion of the descending of the Spirit, and His abiding on these believers on Jesus. Generally, we greatly lack faith in the power of the Spirit of God, and what He can bring about. And yet we get every encouragement. These small gatherings, where the ministry meeting has been maintained, get great encouragement from the Lord, and from the Spirit, and the power that He has. There are not many young men, perhaps, here—I do not know where to put the age limit between the young and the otherwise—but I do trust that such as there are here will listen to see if the Lord has not a word for them this morning as to this very matter, “Your young men shall see visions, and your elders shall dream with dreams”.

So none of us are left out of it, even if we are not so active as the young men. It is a promise, a very ancient promise I may say; I think it is thought that the prophet Joel would be one of the earliest, and the prophecy in its fulness has not come about yet; but what he spoke of has come about so far as to apply to the assembly, to apply to us—and not only to the time when we may be convened for the prophetic meeting; it is possible for it to be characteristic of young men that they see visions. We do not want to be sentimental about it, for everything would be controlled by the Spirit.

You will not see visions unless you are in a state to receive them. And that state would be a state that would be controlled by respect for the Lord Jesus and for the power of the Holy Spirit, so that what you see, and what you put out, would also be governed by the Scriptures, by the word of God. For that you must give yourself to the teaching. I am sure our brother did not mean to belittle the ministry in his remark earlier; no one can afford to belittle the accredited ministries. We need to take in what other men have received and been formed in, and what God has allowed to be recorded and preserved for us.

The same would apply to the elders and their dreams. We do not want mere human imagination, fiction, or phantasies; what we want is the truth, what comes by the Spirit. That is what Peter is saying. The coming of the Spirit affords all this; it affords the word of prophecy. It did so on this outstandingly important day, the day of the coming of the Spirit.
What important times there have been: There was the time of the incoming of the Lord Jesus.

There was the time of His dying. There was the time of His burial. There was the time of His resurrection. There was the time of His ascension, as one says of Him, “He ... has also ascended up above all the heavens” (Ephesians 4: 10), and there is the time of the coming of the Spirit. How great these things are!

Now we are in an important time. In one sense it is midnight, I suppose. It is a most solemn thing to think of the condition of the so-called christian world at the present day. It is almost unbelievable the state of things we have reached in this world. That evil things went on in earlier times, before the flood, there is no doubt. It might be—no one knows—that they were as bad as they are today. They were so bad that God destroyed the whole world

in judgment by the flood. But they are this much worse today—the present state of things is apostasy from Christ. It is certain that God will come in in judgment in various ways before very long; but we are not looking forward to judgment, but to the coming of the Lord for the church, for us as of it—a very great matter; not only the event, but the Person Himself.

Therefore the hour is important; on the one hand the darkness so great—almost unbelievable. Only two days ago I saw an advertisement on a hoarding which was almost unbelievable in a so-called Christian country. On the other hand, the Lord is going to take His own—all of them—out of it very soon. What an important moment we are at and we need to be sustained in view of it; we need to be served to be ready for the Lord as He comes. And the Spirit has the power to endue young men, and old men, and sons and daughters, and bondmen and bondwoman, with the prophetic word, or with whatever is needed at the present time.

My plea, dear brethren, is that we may be exercised to lay ourselves open to receive from the Spirit what is needed in our own localities, and, for some, perhaps a little farther elsewhere besides, if that can be put upon them. The Lord can put upon you something more than your own locality; but you need to serve your own locality first and last—and in between as well. It is not to be at the expense of our own localities, even if some of us go a little farther sometimes.

Well, may the Lord help us! What Peter brought out was the blessed Person of Christ, and all that is in His hand for men—and it was received that very day … as the word came, so the blessing was received—and the next day; and the day after. The last verse of the chapter says, “The Lord added daily”. Day after day it went on. Perhaps it is going on at the present day. The thing is that there should be some increase with each one of us; increase in devotion; increase in love for Christ; increased deliverance from self, so that we consider for one another, and not for self, and, above all, for God. May He help us into it, for His name’s sake.
